([[Teays Valley, West Virginia]]) | college = * [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]] (2021–2022) * [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]] (2022–2023) * [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] (2023–2024) | draft_year = 2024 | career_start = 2024 | career_end = | years1 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]] | team1 = [[Mexico City Capitanes]] | years2 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024–2025]] | team2 = [[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years3 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team3 = Mexico City Capitanes | years4 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team4 = [[San Antonio Spurs]] | years5 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | team5 = →[[Austin Spurs]] | highlights = * [[All-NBA G League Team|NBA G League All-Rookie Team]] ([[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]]) * First-team All-[[American Athletic Conference|AAC]] (2024) }} '''David Apolinar Jones García''' (born 24 November 2001) is a Dominican professional [[basketball]] player for the [[San Antonio Spurs]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul Blue Demons]], [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's Red Storm]], and [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]]. He represents the [[Dominican Republic men's national basketball team|Dominican Republic]] for [[FIBA]] events. ==College career== Jones was noticed by American scouts while representing his native Dominican Republic in FIBA youth tournaments internationally. After performing particularly well in the [[2018 FIBA Under-17 Basketball World Cup|2018 U17 World Cup]], Jones and his family decided he would attend high school in the U.S. as a way to enhance his future professional career. Following his prep career for Teays Valley Christian School in West Virginia, Jones signed with [[DePaul University]] in Chicago.{{cite web|first=Joey|last=Pollizze|title=David Jones' journey leads to bright future|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/article/david-jones-journey-leads-to-bright-future-depaul-blue-demons-basketball--184441998/|website=247Sports.com|publisher=[[247Sports]]|date=14 May 2022|access-date=15 January 2024}} Joining the team for the [[2021 Big East men's basketball tournament|2021 Big East tournament]], Jones played his first full season in 2021–22 and became a starter. On February 9, 2022, Jones recorded the first [[triple-double]] in DePaul program history with 22 points, 14 rebounds and 10 assists in a win over [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]].{{cite web|title=David Jones has DePaul's first-ever triple-double in win over Georgetown|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2022/2/9/22926741/david-jones-has-depaul-first-ever-triple-double-in-win-over-georgetown-hoyas-stubblefield-ongenda|website=SunTimes.com|publisher=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=10 February 2022|access-date=15 January 2024}} After a sophomore campaign where he averaged 14.5 points and 7.4 rebounds per game, Jones chose to transfer, ultimately landing at [[St. John's Red Storm men's basketball|St. John's]]. Jones performed well at St. John's, averaging 13.2 points and 6.8 rebounds, but the season was marred by the death of his father and Jones took time away to attend funeral services in the Dominican Republic.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Fitzpatrick|title=Still grieving, Jones helps St. John's top No. 20 Providence|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-st-johns-red-storm-providence-friars-top-25-college-basketball-today-david-jones-d24724bb207cf8bc5a73964f08843e4e|website=APNews.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=11 February 2023|access-date=15 January 2024}} Following the season and dismissal of coach [[Mike Anderson (basketball, born 1959)|Mike Anderson]] and hiring of [[Rick Pitino]], Jones again entered the transfer portal.{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Braziller|title=David Jones hits transfer portal as St. John's down to three returning players|url=https://nypost.com/2023/04/04/david-jones-is-latest-st-johns-player-to-hit-transfer-portal/|website=NYPost.com|publisher=[[New York Post]]|date=4 April 2023|access-date=15 January 2024}} After considering several schools he committed to coach [[Penny Hardaway]] and the [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis Tigers]].{{cite web|first=Dave|last=Clark|title=David Jones, St. John's transfer who visited Xavier, announces commitment to Memphis|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/xavier/2023/06/05/david-jones-st-johns-transfer-who-visited-xavier-commits-to-memphis-tigers/70291705007/|website=Cincinnati.com|publisher=[[Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=5 June 2023|access-date=15 January 2024}} Jones became the first option of the Tigers' offense for the 2023–24 season. In January 2024, he was named to the [[John R. Wooden Award|Wooden Award]] midseason watch list in recognition of his performance.{{cite web|title=Tigers David Jones named to Wooden Award Midseason Top 25|url=https://wreg.com/sports/tigers-david-jones-named-to-wooden-award-midseason-top-25/|website=wreq.com|publisher=[[Memphis Tigers]]|date=10 January 2024|access-date=15 January 2024}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[2024 NBA draft]], Jones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on 22 July 2024.{{cite web|title=PHILADELPHIA 76ERS SIGN DAVID JONES TO TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-david-jones-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=22 July 2024|access-date=22 July 2024}} However, he was waived on 26 September{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Lester Quinones to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/news/philadelphia-76ers-sign-lester-quinones-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=26 September 2024|access-date=26 September 2024}} and on 28 October, he signed with the [[Mexico City Capitanes]].{{cite tweet|author=Capitanes CDMX|title=Presentando roster para nuestro Training Camp 2024 ⬇️ #EstoEsCapitanes|number=1850907877126598762|user=CapitanesCDMX|date=28 October 2024|access-date=29 October 2024|language=Spanish}} In four games with the Capitanes, Jones García averaged 21.2 points, 6.2 rebounds, and 3.5 assists per game.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Sign David Jones to Two-Way Contract|url= https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-david-jones-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=22 November 2024|access-date=22 November 2024}} On 22 November 2024, Jones was signed to a [[two-way contract]] by the [[Utah Jazz]] of the NBA, splitting time with their G League affiliate, the [[Salt Lake City Stars]]. However, on 1 January 2025, he was waived by the Jazz after only appearing in 13 games for the [[Salt Lake City Stars]],{{cite web|first=Gabby|last=Hundman|title=Utah Jazz Waive David Jones Garcia|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-david-jones-garcia|website=NBA.com|date=1 January 2025|access-date=1 January 2025}} and two days later he rejoined Mexico City.{{cite tweet|author=Capitanes CDMX|title=He's back 🔥🇩🇴 #EstoEsCapitanes|number=1875205594187289036|user=CapitanesCDMX|date=3 January 2025|access-date=3 January 2025|language=Spanish}} Jones participated in the [[2025 NBA Summer League]], and earned All-Summer League first team honors which were announced on July 22, 2025.{{Cite web |date=22 July 2025 |title=NBA 2K26 All-Summer League teams announced |url=https://www.nba.com/news/nba-2k26-all-summer-league-teams-announced |access-date=23 July 2025 |website=nba.com}} On the same day, Jones signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |title=Spurs Sign David Jones Garcia To Two-Way Contract {{!}} San Antonio Spurs |url=https://spurs.com/news/spurssign-david-jones-garcia-to-two-way-contract |access-date=2025-07-23 |website=spurs.com |language=en}} He made 11 appearances for San Antonio during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 2.9 points, 1.2 rebounds, and 1.6 assists. On 4 February 2026, Jones was ruled out for the remainder of the season after undergoing surgery on his right ankle.{{Cite web|title=Spurs injury report: David Jones-Garcia (ankle surgery) out for the season|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/spurs-injury-report-david-jones-002918133.html|access-date=March 4, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} On 22 July 2026, Jones García re–signed with San Antonio on a two–way contract.{{Cite web|title=Spurs move on from young player to continue investing in David Jones-Garcia|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/spurs-move-one-young-player-170951975.html|access-date=August 25, 2026|website=sports.yahoo.com|language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio]] | 11 || 0 || 6.2 || .520 || .600 || .500 || 1.2 || 1.6 || .5 || .1 || 2.9 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 11 || 0 || 6.2 || .520 || .600 || .500 || 1.2 || 1.6 || .5 || .1 || 2.9 {{S-end}} ===Domestic Leagues=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:100%; text-align:right;" !
